documents.title: zcg · methodology
documents.text:
How we compute this · OpenZcash
OpenZcash is a read-only mirror: it never holds spend keys and moves no funds. Every figure comes from public sources. Here is how.
ZCG public spreadsheet
The disbursements ledger, recipient and classification pivots, and ZCG and Coinholder proposal history. Collection is scheduled every six hours. A successful collection does not mean the source was recently edited.
GitHub issue tracker
Live grant applications (ZcashCommunityGrants/zcashcommunitygrants), read first-hand from open issues: applications carry the “Grant Application” label, and “Ready For ZCG Review” marks the queue awaiting the committee's judgement. Hand-filed re-applications can arrive without labels and are recognised by their title; an open application with no decision label counts as awaiting review. This is the rawest stage, before anything reaches the spreadsheet. The issue list is cached for about fifteen minutes.
Zcash Community Forum
ZCG meeting minutes, imported from the Discourse #grants category during the six-hour cycle, best-effort: a failed forum import never marks the collection stale.
On-chain (lightwalletd)

documents.title: zcg · methodology
documents.text:
The Lockbox / ZIP-1016 ZEC balance: the latest spreadsheet Lockbox snapshot plus protocol-deterministic accrual (0.06249999 ZEC per block since NU7 and 0.1875 ZEC before it, ZIP-1015 and ZIP-218) up to the live chain tip, which lightwalletd supplies read-only. No viewing-key scans run. Market prices, grant approvals and milestone delivery are not facts supplied by the chain.
CoinGecko, CoinPaprika, Coinbase
The current ZEC/USD market price from CoinGecko, or from CoinPaprika and then Coinbase when CoinGecko is unavailable, cached for approximately ten minutes; every quote names its provider and quote time. If all three are unavailable, the last cached price or the spreadsheet's recorded rate may be used. This price is not read from the Zcash chain.
How we compute this
Where the data comes from
:
Rule 1 · Source precedence
When sources disagree, the disagreement is published rather than blended, and each figure names the source that wins for it:
Grant payments, budgets and recipient totals
: the official spreadsheet is the primary ledger. OpenZcash mirrors it; it does not correct it.
Proposal status
: a committee decision visible on GitHub is shown until the spreadsheet records the same verdict; once the spreadsheet's verdict is publication-eligible, it takes priority.
Application text and requested amounts
: the GitHub issue is first-hand.
Third-party grant lists

Why the two “discretionary” figures differ
The discretionary budget appears two ways, and the two numbers differ on purpose:
The
figure on the totals split (~$1.8M) comes from the
totals pivot
: the cumulative classification total published in the spreadsheet.
The discretionary
budget tab
($1M annual cap, ~$1.27M spent) is a separate annual worksheet.
Two readings of the same programme at different scopes (cumulative pivot vs. annual budget). That is why the
page shows a live ledger-vs-published cross-check instead of asserting they match.
Rule 3 · USD vs ZEC
Three quantities appear across this site. They describe different things and must not be added together:
Budgeted USD
: includes paid and unpaid entries, including amounts recorded for cancelled grants.
USD paid
: the budgeted value of entries marked paid, not their current market value.
ZEC paid
: the quantity recorded by the spreadsheet, at its own recorded rate.

documents.title: zcg · methodology
documents.text:
Historical ZEC is never revalued at today's price. Treasury USD valuations use the available market price; historical entries keep their recorded rate. The
reconciliation
page shows ZEC paid and USD paid side by side: read them as two columns of one ledger, not one total.
Rule 4 · Payment ≠ delivery
An approval is not a payment. A recorded payment is a ledger entry, not independent proof that a milestone was delivered or that it had impact. Unpaid entries are not necessarily outstanding commitments: check the grant's status and the original source. Cancelled grants remain inside some budgeted totals and are labelled as such.
This is the rule agents quoting these figures repeat: Zarvis and the published ZCG copilot skill state the same thing.
Rule 5 · Reconciliation limits
The transparent treasury reveals aggregate flow only: the Lockbox feeds ZCG's operating treasury, which moves ZEC into the shielded pool. Individual grantee payments leave the shielded pool and are private by design; auditing them one by one would require ZCG's shielded viewing key, which OpenZcash does not hold or use. The cross-check is stored treasury flow plus spreadsheet integrity — never a per-payment on-chain proof. Current figures and the stored scan:
What this page does not claim

How these numbers are calculated
Sources & methodology
Scope.
Volume and swap counts cover the entire ZEC.ZEC pool, including activity before ZCG joined. They do not measure the volume caused by ZCG’s contribution, unique traders or a return on the grant.
Historical volume.
Midgard’s USD cents are converted to dollars without applying today’s prices. The total includes native, trade-asset and synthetic-asset swaps; the breakdown reconciles to that total.
Prices.
The ZCG position values ZEC at the site’s oracle and CACAO at CoinGecko (or a clearly labelled pool-implied fallback). Maya’s internal USD quote can differ.
Earnings.
Net pool earnings and gross fees are different measures. The monthly estimate assumes today’s member units were held throughout each included month. Deposits, withdrawals or changes in units can change that estimate. The sheet’s fee-revenue cell is not used as a zero.
Freshness.
Maya requests are cached for five minutes. Failed requests retain a dated, labelled snapshot when one exists; missing data is shown as unavailable. Zero means the source returned zero. The latest month is incomplete.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 1982 · The idea of untraceable money
documents.text:
Chapter era: 1982
The idea of untraceable money
David Chaum
Long before blockchains, cryptographer David Chaum published “Blind Signatures for Untraceable Payments” (1982): a bank could sign a digital coin without seeing it, so the coin could later be spent without the bank linking it back to you. Digital cash that behaved like cash.
Chaum founded DigiCash in 1989 to build it. Its eCash ran a real pilot at a US bank in 1995, but the company went bankrupt in 1998. The world was not ready, and the money still needed a bank at the center.
One detail matters for this story: in 1996 a computer science student named Zooko Wilcox took a leave of absence to work as a junior coder at DigiCash. The company failed; the apprenticeship did not.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 1992 · The cypherpunks
documents.text:
Chapter era: 1992
The cypherpunks
Hughes, May, Gilmore and a mailing list
In 1992 a mailing list formed around a simple position: privacy in the electronic age would have to be built with code, not requested from institutions. Eric Hughes opened his 1993 manifesto with the line “Privacy is necessary for an open society in the electronic age.”
The list became the proving ground for everything that followed: remailers, digital cash schemes, and the culture of shipping working cryptography instead of position papers. Zooko Wilcox, who later brought Zcash to life, was posting to the list by 1997: an “original cypherpunk,” as Zcash’s own site puts it.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 1997–2004 · The missing pieces
documents.text:
Chapter era: 1997–2004
The missing pieces
Back, Dai, Szabo, Finney
Adam Back’s Hashcash (1997) made computation itself a scarce stamp. Wei Dai’s b-money and Nick Szabo’s bit gold (late 1990s) sketched money without a central issuer. Each solved a piece; none shipped as money.
Hal Finney, veteran cypherpunk and PGP developer, also wrote working code for zero-knowledge proofs. At the rump session of the Crypto ’98 conference in Santa Barbara, on August 25, 1998, he gave a five-minute talk, “A zero-knowledge proof of possession of a pre-image of a SHA-1 hash”: a program that proves you know a message with a given SHA-1 hash without revealing the message, built on a proof system Ronald Cramer and Ivan Damgård presented at the same conference. It was a talk, not a paper, and the session was filmed.
In 2004 Finney built RPOW, reusable proofs of work: tokens minted from hashcash that could pass from person to person. The prototype ran on a central server and never took off. When Bitcoin appeared he was, by his own account, the first person besides its creator to run it, and he received the first Bitcoin transaction ever sent (January 12, 2009).
Finney died in 2014. The problem he spent decades on, private electronic cash that needs no permission, is the problem Zcash exists to finish.
Hal Finney at the Crypto ’98 rump session

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2008–2009 · Bitcoin ships, and exposes everything
documents.text:
Chapter era: 2008–2009
Bitcoin ships, and exposes everything
Satoshi Nakamoto
The Bitcoin whitepaper (October 31, 2008) and genesis block (January 3, 2009) solved decentralized consensus. Money finally worked without a bank.
But it worked in public. Every amount, every counterparty, every balance, forever, on a ledger anyone can read. Bitcoin realized the cypherpunk dream of permissionless money while inverting its premise of privacy.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2009–2010 · The problem Satoshi left open
documents.text:
Chapter era: 2009–2010
The problem Satoshi left open
Satoshi Nakamoto, Zooko Wilcox, Daira-Emma Hopwood
On January 26, 2009, eighteen days after Bitcoin’s first release, Zooko Wilcox wrote a short post on his own blog, Zooko’s Hack Log, about why digital cash had failed at DigiCash and where it might work next. It ends by pointing to bit gold, b-money and “BitCoin by Satoshi Nakamoto.” It is one of the earliest known blog posts to mention Bitcoin, and Zooko has called it the first. By March 2009, bitcoin.org listed “Zooko’s blog” among its related links, beside b-money and bit gold. The link led into Tahoe-LAFS, the decentralized storage system Zooko was building at allmydata: the blog lived on its test grid.
In August 2010 a BitcoinTalk thread asked whether Bitcoin could work without publishing every transaction, and another user suggested zero-knowledge proofs. Satoshi called the problem a very interesting one and said a solution would make a much better Bitcoin possible. He doubted the tool, though: to rule out a double-spend, a node seemed to need to know about every transaction.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2009–2010 · The problem Satoshi left open
documents.text:
In August 2010, two days after his first response in the same BitcoinTalk thread, Satoshi floated “key blinding”, a fresh, unlinkable key for every payment, and pointed to an unfinished draft on recipient-hiding encryption. He named no author. The draft is widely attributed to Daira-Emma Hopwood, writing under a former name. By then Hopwood was also a Tahoe-LAFS developer alongside Zooko, and in 2016 was the first-named author of the Zcash protocol specification.
On August 21, 2010, Tahoe-LAFS began accepting bitcoin donations, and Zooko, signing as the project’s community organizer, opened a thread about building Bitcoin payments into it. Satoshi’s reply left the proposal aside. It opened with Zooko’s name and thanked him, in public, for blogging about Bitcoin back when it was announced on the Cryptography mailing list. His last forum post came that December. In 2022 Zooko pointed back to the August thread: four months later Satoshi was gone, and three years after that, a solution was found.
It's hard to think of how to apply zero-knowledge-proofs in this case.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2013–2014 · Zerocoin, then Zerocash
documents.text:
Chapter era: 2013–2014
Zerocoin, then Zerocash
Johns Hopkins, MIT, Technion, Tel Aviv
Zerocoin (2013, Miers, Garman, Green and Rubin at Johns Hopkins) proposed a cryptographic washing machine bolted onto Bitcoin. Zerocash (2014, Ben-Sasson, Chiesa, Garman, Green, Miers, Tromer and Virza) went further: a full currency where sender, receiver and amount are hidden, yet every transaction is verified.
The tool that made it possible was the zk-SNARK, a succinct proof that a statement is true without revealing why. The proofs predate these papers; Zerocash was the moment they became a payment system on paper. It needed a team willing to make it real.
Zerocoin, IEEE S&P 2013
Zerocash, IEEE S&P 2014

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2016 · The Ceremony
documents.text:
Chapter era: 2016
The Ceremony
Six witnesses, air-gapped machines, one secret guest
Zcash’s original proving system required secret parameters that, if any single party kept them, could be used to counterfeit coins invisibly. So on October 22 and 23, 2016 the launch team ran a multi-party ceremony: six witnesses in separate places, air-gapped hardware, destroyed key material. If even one of them was honest, the combined secret could never be rebuilt.
The stations were paranoia made real. Peter Todd ran his from a rented car on a drive through British Columbia, a trip he called the “Cypherpunk Desert Bus.” At the Denver station, a phone behaved strangely enough mid-ceremony that the moment became a Radiolab story. And one witness, known only as “John Dobbertin,” stayed pseudonymous for six years: in April 2022, Zcash Media revealed he was Edward Snowden.
On October 28, 2016 the genesis block was mined. That day, in a thin early market on the Poloniex exchange, one ZEC briefly reached roughly 3,300 BTC, and it still traded at 48 BTC later in the day, CoinDesk reported. The experiment was live.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2016 · Launch
documents.text:
Year: 2016
Launch
Oct 28 · Genesis
Mainnet launches with Sprout shielded transactions, a 21M cap, 2.5-minute blocks and a 12.5 ZEC subsidy, ramped in over a 34-day slow start. The Founders’ Reward directs 20% of the subsidy to the founding team, investors and the Zcash Foundation for the first four years, 10% of total supply.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2018 · The quiet save, then Sapling
documents.text:
Year: 2018
The quiet save, then Sapling
Mar 1 · A flaw found
Ariel Gabizon finds a flaw in the proving system Sprout used that could have allowed invisible counterfeiting. It is fixed quietly by the Sapling upgrade in October and disclosed in February 2019. No evidence of exploitation was ever found.
Oct 28 · Sapling
A redesign of shielded transactions cuts proving time and memory sharply, making shielded payments practical on phones. It ships on the network’s second birthday, on parameters from a new, larger ceremony.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2019 · Blossom
documents.text:
Year: 2019
Blossom
Dec 11 · 75-second blocks
Block time drops from 150 to 75 seconds and the per-block subsidy from 12.5 to 6.25 ZEC, keeping issuance per hour unchanged. It is why the first halving lands on 3.125, not 6.25.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2020 · First halving and the Dev Fund
documents.text:
Year: 2020
First halving and the Dev Fund
Jul · Heartwood
Shielded coinbase: miners can receive block rewards directly into shielded addresses.
Nov 18 · Canopy, the first halving
The subsidy halves to 3.125 ZEC. The Founders’ Reward ends and ZIP 1014’s Dev Fund begins: 7% to Bootstrap (ECC), 5% to the Zcash Foundation and 8% to Major Grants, run by ZOMG and renamed Zcash Community Grants in February 2022.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2022 · NU5: no more ceremonies
documents.text:
Year: 2022
NU5: no more ceremonies
May 31 · Orchard and Halo 2
The Halo 2 proving system removes the trusted setup for the new Orchard pool, and Unified Addresses bundle transparent, Sapling and Orchard receivers into one address.
Jun · Sandblasting
A sustained spam attack bloats the chain and exposes wallet sync pain. It forces the fee overhaul of ZIP 317 and a generation of faster sync work.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2024 · Second halving and the lockbox
documents.text:
Year: 2024
Second halving and the lockbox
2023–2024 · New stewards
Zooko hands the ECC CEO role to Josh Swihart in December 2023. Zashi ships as ECC’s mobile wallet in 2024, while Zebra, the Foundation’s Rust node, reaches production alongside zcashd.
Nov 23 · NU6, the second halving
The subsidy halves to 1.5625 ZEC. 8% goes to Zcash Community Grants, paid to the Financial Privacy Foundation, and 12%, 0.1875 ZEC per block, accrues in an in-protocol lockbox.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2025 · Coinholders take the wheel
documents.text:
Year: 2025
Coinholders take the wheel
Nov 24 · NU6.1
The lockbox pays its 78,750 ZEC to a coinholder-controlled fund, and the 8% and 12% streams continue to the third halving (ZIP 271, ZIP 1016). Coinholders now vote on grants from the fund; key-holders sign the payouts.

documents.title: ceremony · road · 2026 · The Orchard emergency, then year ten
documents.text:
Year: 2026
The Orchard emergency, then year ten
Mar 16 · A veto
Two key-holders, the Zcash Foundation and Shielded Labs, announce a veto of the $2.67M Q4 2025 grant to Bootstrap (ECC), approved by coinholders months earlier.
Jun 2–3 · The Orchard emergency
A soundness flaw in the Orchard circuit leads to an emergency soft fork that disables Orchard at block 3,363,426; the NU6.2 network upgrade at block 3,364,600 re-enables it with a corrected circuit (ZIP 257).
Jul 28 · Ironwood
NU6.3 activates at block 3,428,143 with a new shielded pool, Ironwood (ZIP 258). Orchard stops taking new funds, and balances move out into Ironwood.
Sep 14 · NU7’s scope
Coinholders vote to keep the halvings, retire v4 transactions at NU7 and move to 25-second blocks; 2.4M ZEC took part in the first question. They also back reissuance from February 2031, but coinholder and community polls reach no shared majority on the date, and NU7 takes 2031 as the more conservative choice.
Oct 28 · Ten years
Ten years since the genesis block.

documents.title: ceremony · road
documents.text:
“The reward halved from 12.5 to 6.25 in 2020”
No. Blossom (2019) moved to 75-second blocks and 6.25 ZEC per block with unchanged hourly issuance. The 2020 halving went to 3.125, and 2024 to 1.5625.
“Zerocash created zk-SNARKs”
Zero-knowledge proofs date to 1985, and the first known SNARK construction, Micali’s CS proofs, to 1994; the zk-SNARKs Zerocash used come from the early 2010s. Zerocash was the first full payment design built on them, hiding sender, receiver and amount; Zcash made it run in production.
“Zcash is governed by a DAO”
There is no Zcash DAO. Decisions run through the ZIP process, ZCAP and coinholder polls, coinholder votes on the fund (ZIP 1016) and independent organizations. ZecHub runs a DAO, and it governs a community project, not the protocol.
“ZOMG runs the Major Grants”
Not since February 2022, when Zcash Open Major Grants was renamed Zcash Community Grants. It still funds independent teams doing major ongoing development; since NU6 in November 2024 its stream is paid to the Financial Privacy Foundation.

documents.title: Zcash Pitches & Narratives · Send the money. Keep your space. · 30s
documents.text:
Audience: beginners.
For everyday payments, shared expenses and first conversations about Zcash.
The payment can travel. Your personal life does not have to travel with it.
Zcash brings a simple expectation to digital money: a payment can reach another person without putting its private details on public display. Para equipes, organizações e pessoas que precisam compartilhar informações financeiras com responsabilidade.
Guardar um registro e publicá-lo para o mundo são duas decisões diferentes.
Zcash separa a possibilidade de visualizar certas informações de pagamento da permissão para gastar, oferecendo às equipes formas mais conscientes de compartilhar acesso financeiro. Uma equipe pode precisar que alguém examine registros sem controlar os fundos. Chaves de visualização podem apoiar essa separação. É um bom ponto de partida para falar de privacidade e prestação de contas: definir quem precisa de acesso, entender o que a chave revela e separar a autoridade para gastar.

O objetivo é uma política de acesso bem pensada, sem um fluxo público de todas as transações. Teste a carteira e o tipo exato de chave antes de criar um processo de prestação de contas.
Confira o alcance antes de compartilhar. Uma chave pode expor um histórico amplo e atividades futuras, e informações já vistas não podem ser recolhidas. O acesso, sozinho, não resolve todas as obrigações de prestação de contas.

documents.title: Zcash Pitches & Narratives · library size / quantos / cuántos
documents.text: The library contains 20 original pitches and 8 narrative themes. documents.title: Zcash Pitches & Narratives · using the library
documents.text: Original OpenZcash educational copy in English, Brazilian Portuguese and Spanish. Choose Pitches for examples or Narratives for the underlying ideas. Each pitch has a one-sentence, approximately 30-second and approximately 60-second version. Search the current language and filter by audience and theme. Prepare a pitch selects an existing reviewed example; it does not generate a new AI response. Copy text copies the selected version; Copy link opens that example with its language and length. Expand Make it your own for context and limitations. The library has no Sources tab or external reference links.

documents.title: Zcash Pitches & Narratives · select and print / imprimir / impresión
documents.text: In Pitches, check Select for printing on a card. Selected cards gain a gold outline and a Selected for printing label. Selecting does not open printing. After selecting at least one card, click the yellow Print selected button with the selection count in the results toolbar. It calls the browser print dialog, where Save as PDF may be available. Printing uses the selected pitches with the current language and length, including previously selected pitches that later become hidden when filters change. A hidden card cannot be selected until filters make it visible again. Clear selection removes the selections. Selection is held in page memory and is not saved in a copied link or across reloads. If an embedded browser does not show its print dialog, open the same page in a browser that supports printing and select the cards again.

documents.title: Zcash Pitches & Narratives · idiomas, filtros, copiar e imprimir
documents.text: A biblioteca tem textos originais em inglês, português brasileiro e espanhol. Pitches reúne exemplos de uma frase, cerca de 30 segundos ou cerca de 60 segundos. Narrativas explica a ideia, os fundamentos e os limites. A busca usa o idioma selecionado; os filtros selecionam público e tema. Preparar um pitch escolhe um exemplo existente. Copiar texto copia a versão atual; Copiar link abre esse exemplo no idioma e extensão escolhidos. Para imprimir, marque Selecionar para impressão; o cartão ganha contorno dourado. Depois clique no botão amarelo Imprimir selecionados. Marcar não abre a impressão. O navegador abre seu diálogo; salvar como PDF depende dele. Selecione um cartão enquanto ele está visível. Se um filtro depois esconder esse cartão, ele continua selecionado para impressão. Para selecionar um cartão oculto, primeiro ajuste os filtros para mostrá-lo. A seleção não fica no link e se perde ao recarregar. Não há aba Sources ou links externos de referências. Se um navegador embutido não abrir o diálogo, abra a página em um navegador com suporte à impressão e selecione os cartões novamente.

Después pulsa el botón amarillo Imprimir seleccionados. Marcar no abre la impresión. El navegador muestra su diálogo y puede permitir guardar como PDF. Selecciona una tarjeta mientras está visible. documents.title: Crosslink · Ongoing Test · testing, cTAZ and incentives
documents.text: The Crosslink guide has Participate, Community tools and Incentives tabs. Participate offers Test, Build and Operate paths. Test uses a separate test wallet and cTAZ only: install and privately back up, sync, compare a block height AND hash on the same network, get test funds, choose a finalizer and stake, retarget a bond, then unbond and withdraw in allowed windows. Check advancing finalized height too. Record build, OS, time, transaction IDs and expected versus actual behavior; never include keys or seeds. Listed community issues are not assignments or promised funding. Incentive allocations, earned rewards, claims and reported payouts are different states. Curated release and round notes are dated snapshots; confirm current compatibility and claim windows in the linked program sources. Test cTAZ is not mainnet ZEC.

documents.title: ZCG Participate · community proposals and demo Zcred
documents.text: Participate lets visitors explore proposals and discuss ideas with a verifiable history. Participation uses free demo Zcred. Demo participation, community feedback and an official committee decision are separate. A committee verdict does not establish payment or delivered work. Zarvis reads public records only; it cannot see private drafts or committee workspace records, post comments, submit applications, spend credits or vote on the visitor's behalf. Public applications, decisions and payment records must be checked with their respective readers and dates.

documents.title: Private Chat · Nym experimental pilot
documents.text: OpenZcash links to an experimental Private Chat pilot using Nym. The page hosts an isolated chat service inside the site. This is a separate service from Zarvis. Zarvis has no access to its rooms, messages or identities. A pilot label does not establish a security audit, universal anonymity, uptime or suitability for a particular threat model. Consult the service's own current interface for its available features.

documents.title: Zarvis · knowledge, tests, system and capabilities
documents.text: Zarvis answers questions about Zcash and OpenZcash using reviewed references, indexed public pages and read-only tools. Static documentation describes workflows; live tools return data with freshness and coverage. It does not read the whole repository, internal test reports, private committee workspaces, deployment dashboards or wallets. A source revision, editorial review date or local preview does not prove tests passed, a PR merged or a production release succeeded. For build, test and publication status it needs current evidence for that exact version; without that evidence the status is unverified. It can draft original pitches adapted to an audience, occasion, channel, language and length, grounded in the library; a draft is not a new verified fact. Reloading clears chat memory. Model answers send recent context and retrieved public records to the configured provider. Availability and limits are shown on /zarvis/about.

documents.title: Zarvis guide · badges, try-these questions, answer anatomy, depth
documents.text: The interactive guide at /zarvis/guide teaches the Zarvis chat by showing it. Live badge samples rendered by the same code as the chat say where an answer came from: Direct from OpenZcash data · no AI, or a model answer naming the model and counting its sources. Try these questions links open /zarvis with the composer pre-filled; nothing is sent until the visitor presses send. An annotated sample answer marks the badge, the sources list, the withheld-figure notice and the copy/share actions. Quick answers are written within 55 seconds and Deep analysis within 110; quotas, retention and limits stay on /zarvis/about.

documents.title: Coinholder Grants · Proposals
documents.text: The permanent Proposals page at /coinholders/proposals shows the current round, Q4 2026. It lists open applications from the Financial-Privacy-Foundation/ZcashCoinholderGrantsProgram GitHub repository with the exact label Ready For Vote - All Steps Completed, created from October 30 through December 31, 2026. If FPF provisionally retains a hidden application, its entry links the public forum decision. Decided, withdrawn and cancelled applications are excluded. Search by title, applicant or organization, filter by category and sort by amount or date. View proposal opens the details and links the application source on GitHub or the forum. Requested amounts reflect applicants' latest edits. The FPF schedule accepts proposals October 30–November 13, reviews November 16–December 16 and schedules voting December 17–29, 2026. Each closing deadline is 20:00 UTC. Official submission status is not approval, payment or a vote result. Counts, requested USD and labels are checked on access with a five-minute cache. A stale or unavailable source is marked explicitly; an unavailable source does not mean zero proposals. This static guide cannot establish current proposal counts or funding totals; consult the page and its last successful check. Sources & method contains the exact eligibility label and source link. The page refreshes every five minutes while visible; Refresh also checks the current cached list. Results, Voting activity and Verify default to the active cycle, Q4 2026, with a pending state and the same announced timeline. Q3 and earlier outcomes are selected by round; activity archives currently cover Q3 2026 only. Q4 has no published result, vote-chain tally or verification yet. The program overview and fund show the current cycle separately from historical approvals and payments. FPF announces quarterly cycles; later dates are not inferred automatically.

documents.title: Zcash Opportunities: quests, bounties, jobs and testing
documents.text: OpenZcash Opportunities is an ecosystem directory. It links visitors to Gleyo quests and communities, public ZEC Bounties tasks, Yukon HashSmash challenges, Shielded Labs Crosslink testing and incentives, and official careers pages. OpenZcash does not run these programs or accept applications, submissions, payments or registrations. A read-only server import shows approved, public, unassigned, unexpired mainnet ZEC Bounties records, refreshed on access with a fifteen-minute cache. Source failures are marked; curated links remain available. The default listing order is mixed for each visit. Filters include type, platform, language and country; missing locale information is not inferred. The 29 matte-paper stock covers can be selected and downloaded. Prepare activity assembles a local brief using Gleyo or ZEC Bounties fields, offers text copying and cover download, and directs the user to publish on the chosen platform. It does not create an account, reserve funds or publish a bounty. Quests may offer XP without ZEC. HashSmash follows Yukon rules and has no additional OpenZcash monthly prize. Crosslink links to /ongoing-test/crosslink?tab=incentives. Job availability and application requirements must be confirmed with each employer. The earlier illustrative tasks and rewards were retired. Preparacao local de arte e texto, com cadastro e participacao somente na plataforma de origem.

documents.title: OpenZcash Treasury · voluntary donations, public viewing key and contributions
documents.text: OpenZcash Treasury is the project's own community-supported treasury, separate from ZCG and Coinholder program funds. The owner-supplied mainnet donation address and public full viewing key are available with copy controls and a QR generated locally from the exact address. Amounts and recoverable text memos are public; donors should not include personal information in memos. A memo reading "For Michae2xl: retroactive work" designates a donation to Michae2xl for work already delivered; donations without that note go to maintenance and improvements. A separate local watch-only worker scans the account and publishes reconciled snapshots to a read-only GET API. The page refreshes every 15 seconds, showing confirmed balance, net incoming and outgoing movements, recoverable memos, sync block and UTC time. Outflows include network fees; internal pool transfers are netted. Missing data stays unavailable and older or failed updates are labeled. The dedicated Vizor account was created on 2026-11-10; the scan starts before that date. A local preview does not establish a public scanner deployment. MIT source release is planned without a grant; public release is in preparation. OpenZcash will not apply for a grant for itself, neither to ZCG nor to the Coinholder retroactive grants. Contributor incentives depend on available funds, with a published scope, budget and acceptance criteria. Read the open letter at /openzcash-treasury/letter, published in English. Opportunities leads to the Crosslink guide.

documents.title: OpenZcash · open letter, open source, donations and a public treasury
documents.text: Open letter on the continuity of OpenZcash: it expresses pride in the pioneering work with Zarvis and the copilots, Zcash's funding history in Since block zero and the governance tools. OpenZcash will not apply for a grant for itself, neither to ZCG nor to the Coinholder retroactive grants. The commitment is to release the code under MIT, receive voluntary donations in a dedicated wallet and share its viewing key with the community. The address and public viewing key are on the Treasury page, with balance and history shown only once the scan has been synchronized and reconciled. The key cannot spend funds and may reveal amounts and memos. A donation whose public memo designates Michae2xl for work already delivered is treated as such; donations without that note go to maintenance and improvements. The letter is signed by Michae2xl. Publication of the code is still in preparation. Contributor incentives will depend on available resources, with scope, budget and acceptance criteria set beforehand. The letter is published in English and links back to OpenZcash Treasury.
